pattern: DDD: ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, context map
implementation_contract: Owned schemas and vocabulary; integrate through contracts.

pattern: DDD: entities, value objects, aggregates, invariant enforcement
implementation_contract: Money/Quantity/IDs; aggregate methods, factories, and explicit transitions.

pattern: DDD: domain services, policies/specifications, domain events
implementation_contract: Pure eligibility/pricing policies and past-tense events; decisions stay out of transport.

pattern: Anti-corruption layer and published language
implementation_contract: Translate provider and extracted-service types; no shared private domain objects.

pattern: Vertical slices and use-case handlers
implementation_contract: Command/query DTO, handler, validation, ports, and tests grouped by feature.

pattern: Ports/adapters and explicit composition roots
implementation_contract: Use small interfaces at actual I/O seams, not an interface for every struct.

pattern: Modular monolith and deliberate service extraction
implementation_contract: Contract-compatible process modes with one writer owner during extraction.

pattern: Repository/data mapper and unit of work
implementation_contract: Aggregate-focused persistence plus scoped transaction runner; no generic CRUD framework.

pattern: CQRS and materialized projections
implementation_contract: Separate write models and rebuildable query schemas with freshness contracts.

pattern: Event sourcing, snapshots, and event upcasting
implementation_contract: Authoritative validated events, expected version, deterministic replay, versioned snapshots.

pattern: Transactional outbox and reliable publisher
implementation_contract: Business change and event intent in one transaction; at-least-once publication.

pattern: Transactional inbox and idempotent consumer
implementation_contract: Inbox uniqueness and effects commit together; dedup retention covers replay.

pattern: Sagas, process managers, and compensating actions
implementation_contract: Orchestrated checkout and limited choreography example with explicit recovery.

pattern: Durable execution, activity retries, workflow versioning
implementation_contract: Temporal and explicit persisted process-manager alternatives share outcome tests.

pattern: Request idempotency and end-to-end duplicate suppression
implementation_contract: Scoped key, request hash, stable response, provider key, and reconciliation.

pattern: Publish/subscribe, competing consumers, routing, request/reply
implementation_contract: Executable broker patterns with delivery/ordering contracts.

pattern: Message filter, enrichment, splitter/aggregator, scatter/gather
implementation_contract: Bounded state and explicit correlation, ordering, and partial-result behavior.

pattern: Dead-letter/quarantine and controlled replay
implementation_contract: Preserve original identity; poison ordering-sensitive events pause their stream.

pattern: Optimistic concurrency and compare-and-set
implementation_contract: Versioned writes and full-operation retry on conflict.

pattern: Pessimistic locking and serializable transactions
implementation_contract: Use real database guarantees and test the actual invariant.

pattern: Distributed atomic commit and in-doubt recovery
implementation_contract: 2PC/XA exercise, bounded 3PC alternative, blocking behavior made observable.

pattern: CDC, ETL, and incremental view maintenance
implementation_contract: Snapshot/WAL handoff, lineage, versioned transforms, rebuildability.

pattern: Cache-aside, read-through, refresh-ahead, negative caching
implementation_contract: Add read-through/refresh-ahead wrappers as comparison adapters; define staleness bounds.

pattern: Write-through/write-behind and cache invalidation
implementation_contract: Comparison labs demonstrate write-behind loss and ordering risks; authoritative path remains explicit.

pattern: Singleflight, TTL jitter, and hot-key protection
implementation_contract: Bound regeneration work and isolate noisy tenants.

pattern: Deadlines, cancellation, bounded retries, exponential backoff/jitter
implementation_contract: Propagate one end-to-end budget; only retry operations with safe identity semantics.

pattern: Circuit breaker, bulkhead, rate limit, admission control
implementation_contract: Protect finite resources and test recovery after dependency failure.

pattern: Backpressure, bounded queues, worker pools, graceful drain
implementation_contract: Own goroutine lifetimes and shutdown order; no unbounded buffers.

pattern: Leader election, leases, fencing, and work allocation
implementation_contract: Linearizable allocator plus resource-enforced token check.

pattern: Replication, session consistency, and read routing
implementation_contract: Explicit primary/replica read contracts and stale-read remedies.

pattern: Sharding, consistent hashing, and safe resharding
implementation_contract: Epoch-based ownership, snapshot/catch-up/cutover, resumable migration.

pattern: CRDTs, conflict resolution, and offline synchronization
implementation_contract: Convergence under declared semantics; never substitute for scarce-resource coordination.

pattern: Append-only journal, reconciliation, and auditable correction
implementation_contract: Balanced immutable postings and independent integrity checks.

pattern: Expand/contract migration, backfill, and versioned schemas
implementation_contract: Mixed-version compatibility, resumable backfill, explicit rollback window.

pattern: Shadow projection, blue/green data generation, atomic cutover
implementation_contract: Consistency barrier and checksums before changing reader generation.

pattern: Branch by abstraction, strangler migration, feature flags
implementation_contract: Controlled routing, one owner, compatible rollback and flag retirement.

pattern: REST/OpenAPI, gRPC, GraphQL, gateway composition
implementation_contract: Versioned contracts, bounded requests, conditional writes/ETags, keyset pagination.

pattern: OIDC, RBAC, tenant isolation, least-privilege adapters
implementation_contract: Authentication and per-resource authorization on every transport and data export.

pattern: Telemetry, SLOs, health checks, and error budgets
implementation_contract: Integrity and freshness measured separately; readiness is not liveness.

pattern: Rolling/canary deployment, rollback, and infrastructure as code
implementation_contract: Migrate compatibly, promote tested images, and verify database-aware rollback.

pattern: Backup/PITR, disaster recovery, and game days
implementation_contract: Restore evidence and RPO/RTO measurement; replicas do not replace backups.

pattern: Contract tests, property tests, fuzzing, and deterministic simulation
implementation_contract: Model and real-system evidence plus repeatable seeds and minimized failures.

pattern: Batch DAGs, shuffle, checkpointing, and atomic output publication
implementation_contract: Retryable tasks with immutable outputs and versioned manifests.

pattern: Temporal joins, watermarks, and late-data correction
implementation_contract: Explicit event-time contracts and bounded state.

pattern: Consent, erasure, retention, data minimization
implementation_contract: Purpose-specific processing and replay/backup deletion controls.

pattern: Strategy, adapter, decorator, factory, and functional options in Go
implementation_contract: Concrete uses for routing/merge policies, providers, telemetry/retry, aggregate construction, and validated configuration.

pattern: State machine and durable process orchestration
implementation_contract: Explicit legal transitions, persisted progress, compensations, and recovery states.

pattern: Producer/consumer pipelines and structured Go concurrency
implementation_contract: context cancellation, errgroup-style lifetimes, semaphores, ownership, bounded channels, race/leak checks.
